items.name: C#
items.description: Object-oriented, statically typed programming language developed by Microsoft for the .NET platform, used to build web, desktop, mobile, and game applications.

items.name: COBOL
items.description: Older procedural programming language designed for business and administrative data processing, still widely used in legacy mainframe systems in banking and government.

items.name: Dart
items.description: Object-oriented programming language developed by Google, primarily used with the Flutter framework to build cross-platform mobile, web, and desktop applications.

items.name: Go
items.description: Statically typed, compiled programming language created at Google, valued for its simplicity and built-in support for concurrency; commonly used for backend services and infrastructure tooling.

items.name: Groovy
items.description: Dynamic programming language that runs on the Java Virtual Machine and interoperates closely with Java, often used for scripting, testing, and build automation such as Gradle.

items.name: Java
items.description: Object-oriented, platform-independent programming language widely used for enterprise systems, Android app development, and large-scale backend services.

items.name: Kotlin
items.description: Statically typed programming language that runs on the JVM and interoperates with Java, officially supported by Google as a primary language for Android development.

items.name: Lua
items.description: Lightweight, embeddable scripting language commonly used to add configurable logic and extensibility to applications and video games.

items.name: MATLAB
items.description: Numerical computing environment and programming language used for matrix operations, data analysis, algorithm prototyping, and engineering simulations.

items.name: PL/SQL
items.description: Oracle's procedural extension of SQL, used to write stored procedures, functions, and triggers that implement business logic inside Oracle databases.

items.name: Python
items.description: High-level, general-purpose programming language known for its readable syntax, widely used for web development, data science, automation, and scripting.

items.name: R
items.description: Programming language and environment focused on statistical computing and graphics, commonly used for data analysis and academic research.

items.name: Scratch
items.description: Block-based visual programming language and online platform designed to teach programming concepts to children and beginners.

items.name: Solidity
items.description: Statically typed programming language designed for writing smart contracts that run on the Ethereum blockchain and compatible platforms.

items.name: SQL
items.description: Standard programming language used to query, update, and manage data stored in relational database systems.

items.name: Swift
items.description: Statically typed, compiled programming language developed by Apple for building applications on iOS, macOS, and other Apple platforms.

items.name: Transact-SQL
items.description: Microsoft's procedural extension of SQL used in SQL Server and Azure SQL Database for querying data and implementing stored procedures and triggers.

items.name: VB.NET
items.description: Object-oriented programming language on the .NET platform, evolved from classic Visual Basic, used mainly for building Windows desktop and enterprise applications.

items.name: VBA
items.description: Scripting language embedded in Microsoft Office applications, used to automate repetitive tasks and build custom functionality within documents and spreadsheets.

items.name: Visual Basic
items.description: Event-driven programming language and development environment originally created by Microsoft for building Windows applications with a simplified, beginner-friendly syntax.
